units.translation: 467. Lady goddess Perseis: some say she is the daughter of Zeus, but in the Orphic poems she is traced to Demeter (fr. 41 Kern): 'And then Deo bore Hecate, daughter of a noble father.' Bacchylides says she is the daughter of Night (fr. 40 B. III 583 = 31 Blass-Snell): 'Hecate, torch-bearer, daughter of great-bosomed Night'; Musaeus (cf. 2 B 16 Diels-Kranz) says she is the daughter of Asteria and Zeus, and Pherecydes (3 fr. 44 J.) says she is the daughter of Aristaeus, son of Paeon.
10 δᾳδοφόρε in K : δαϊδοφόρε in L : δαϊφόρου in P : δαδοφόρου in F; μελανοκόλπου Ursinus Carm. IX ill. fem. et lyr. 1568, 342
12 Παιῶνος Wil. ad l. : Παίωνος in P : Παίονος in L
470. 〈Because:〉 because I do not rejoice in evils. The speech is erotic. Lm (P)
471. ἐόλητο: was disturbed and was in anguish. LmP
15 Et. Gen. (B) ἐόλητο: that which has been moved and disturbed. It is also written with the diphthong αι. III 471. cf. W 75
15 ἐόλητο in P : αἰόλητο in L in the poet's words
474. 〈Then indeed Jason:〉 it is a hyperbaton; for Argus addressed Jason. Lm
17 προσεῖπεν in K : -έειπεν
482. ἀντιβολήσων: about to meet; it ends in 'I will converse with, I will arrange with.' Lm (P)
485. O good friend: O sweetest, most pleasant, most beloved, since the ripe fruit is also honey-sweet. LmP
22 μελιχρός W : μελίχρους
486. 〈βάσκετε:〉 it is also written βάσκ’ ἴθι. Lm
490. 〈παρεόντας:〉 Jason and those with him. Lg
492-94a. 〈ἀντικρύ:〉 most openly and most opposed. Lg
b. διειρομένοισι: to those inquiring or speaking. For the sense is contrary to us; for it is not going to be accomplished either by me 〈...〉 of the things commanded.
27 K indicates a lacuna, where F supplies λέγοντι οὔτε ὑμῖν ἐρευνῶσι
497. ἐφίετο: was commanding. LgP
500-01. ὃ δή νύ οἱ: the order is: which I promised him briefly; for there was nothing else better to consider. L
502. 〈ἀνήνυτος:〉 hard to accomplish. Lg
510. πεφυλαγμένος ἐντύναιο: guarding your promise, prepare yourself; for ἐντύνω means 'I prepare'.
511. The ἑή is wrong; for it is third person. It should be σῆ. Lm (P)
7 σῆ Steph. : σήν in L : omitted in P
513-14. οὐ γὰρ ἔγωγε σχήσομαι: instead of 'I will not endure.' For what more awaits me than death? L
8 ἀφέξομαι Herwerden Mnem. N. S. 11, 1883, 116
515-21. Apollonius says that these chose to yoke the oxen, but the Naupactica (fr. 5 Kink.) enumerates all the heroes brought by him.
11 ποιήσας added after Ναυπ. in P; ὑπ’ Ἀργοῦς Robert Die griech. Heldensage 1921, 795 n. 2
523-24. ἀλλὰ τιν’ οἴω μητρὸς ἐμῆς: he says, my mother is able to persuade Medea to help with the contest. But in the Naupactica (fr. 6 Kink.) Idmon stood up and urged Jason to undertake the contest.
529. δάε: taught. LgP
